article_title: Aaditya Thackeray blames road contractors for Mumbai monsoon woes
publish_date: Updated On: 02 July, 2026 09:26 AM IST | Mumbai | Sanjeev Shivadekar
author: Sanjeev Shivadekar
short_description: Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Aaditya Thackeray accused road contractors of poor-quality work, saying it caused waterlogging, potholes and traffic congestion during Mumbai's first spell of monsoon rain
image_caption: Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Aaditya Thackeray during the Maharashtra Monsoon Assembly Session at Vidhan Bhavan. Pic/Sayyed Sameer Abedi
article_content: Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Aaditya Thackeray on Wednesday blamed road contractors for the problems faced by Mumbaikars during the first spell of the monsoon. He said poor-quality road work and the lack of action against contractors led to waterlogging, potholes, and traffic jams across the city, causing hardship to thousands of commuters.

article_title: Mumbai residents raise alarm over potholes, garbage, dark roads and civic neglect
publish_date: Updated On: 17 August, 2026 08:02 AM IST | Mumbai | Team mid-day
author: Team mid-day
short_description: Mumbaikars have raised concerns over dark roads, garbage, potholes, waterlogging, unsafe government premises and alleged encroachment across the city. Civic authorities have responded to some complaints, promising inspections and repairs, while other issues remain pending
article_content:
Problems

Dark roads

Even though the road from Aarey Check Naka to Royal Palms Gate in Goregaon East falls under the BMC, there are no streetlights installed here, which is very dangerous at night. As a resident of Royal Palms, earlier the road ownership was not clear, and hence we did not have access to streetlights. But now, post the court ruling, the BMC has taken ownership, so it should restore the old street lights or install new ones.
Aditya Bahulekar

article_title: Mid-day asks the Govt: Outside BKC Metro, the meter stops and the overcharging begins
publish_date: Updated On: 03 August, 2026 08:16 AM IST | Mumbai | Team mid-day
author: Team mid-day
short_description: Passengers stepping out of Metro stations near JioWorld BKC allege being forced to pay inflated autorickshaw fares instead of metered rates. Commuters claim organised groups of drivers demand exorbitant amounts, intimidate those who object and exploit office-goers and visitors. mid-day asks the authorities: when will the crackdown begin
article_content:
Problems

Rickshaw mafia at Metro exits, BKC

Under Metro stations and right in front of JioWorld BKC, certain autorickshaw drivers operate like a mafia. They refuse meter fares, demand inflated fares, and pressure passengers the moment they step out. What should cost Rs 40-Rs 60 suddenly becomes Rs 150 or more. Argue, and you face aggression or delay.  These organised groups target hurried office-goers, visitors, and seniors who just want a quick ride. Can the authorities please clamp down on these drivers?
Keith Stephen Tauro
